# PostCompass

> PostCompass is a free, open-source (MIT) desktop GUI for PostgreSQL on Windows, macOS and Linux. It can install and run a local PostgreSQL server in one click without Docker or admin rights, connect to cloud PostgreSQL providers, and browse, edit and query data in a native app built with Rust and Tauri.

Key facts:

- Price: free, no account, no paid tier. License: MIT.
- Platforms: Windows 10/11 (x64), macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Linux x86_64 (AppImage, .deb, .rpm).
- Install with one command: `curl -fsSL https://www.postcompass.cloud/install.sh | sh` (macOS, Linux) or `irm https://www.postcompass.cloud/install.ps1 | iex` (Windows PowerShell).
- Local PostgreSQL: versions 14 to 18, official binaries verified by SHA-256, run as the current user, listening only on 127.0.0.1.
- Detects PostgreSQL already installed or running on the computer and connects to it.
- Cloud presets: AWS RDS / Aurora, Google Cloud SQL, Azure Database for PostgreSQL, Alibaba Cloud, Oracle Cloud, DigitalOcean, Heroku Postgres, Neon, Railway, Render, Cloudflare Hyperdrive, or any PostgreSQL server. TLS modes: Off, Prefer, Require, Verify certificate.
- Privacy: no telemetry; passwords stored in the OS keychain.
- Installer size: about 3 to 5 MB (.exe, .dmg, .deb, .rpm); the Linux AppImage is larger because it bundles its own libraries.
